provenanceNote: Half 1 was EXECUTED against the installed SDK (backend/src/__tests__/space-id-derivation.test.ts calls the real makePkhSpaceId/buildSpaceUri/parseSpaceUri and asserts determinism, canonicalization and round-trip). Half 2 is static analysis of the shipped dist: node_modules/@tinycloud/node-sdk/dist/core-ojeY-wet.d.ts:676-722 (the DelegatedAccess class) and dist/core.js:1273-1275 (the spaceId getter body). No live node session was needed for either half, which is itself part of the answer.

deterministicDerivation.api: makePkhSpaceId(address, chainId, name) — also reachable as buildSpaceUri(did:pkh, name)
deterministicDerivation.notes: Pure, synchronous, in-process. Address case is canonicalized (EIP-55 checksum), so a lowercase and a checksummed address derive the SAME id; chainId is validated and an empty name throws. parseSpaceUri round-trips it back to {owner: did:pkh, chainId, address, name}. This is exactly the comparand §9.2's (F)-branch control needs on the right-hand side, derived from the SESSION's address rather than fetched from any endpoint.

activatedAccessExposesResolvedSpaceId.answer: no — it exposes an ECHO, not a resolution
activatedAccessExposesResolvedSpaceId.notes: The getter returns the spaceId field of the PortableDelegation the caller passed in — the same unsigned, attacker-rewritable top-level field §9.2 exists to stop trusting. It is not the space the node resolved the invocation into; nothing in the class records that, and useDelegation performs no node round trip at all (dist/core.js:5056 compares delegateDID against our own DID and constructs DelegatedAccess locally). So reading access.spaceId back and comparing it to a derived id compares the derived id against the attacker's own input.

consequence: R10 requires BOTH halves to be yes before §9.2's (F)-branch owner-binding control may be built. Half 2 is no, so per R10 the answer is the escape hatch, NOT a weaker probe: escalate to the operator, whose honest options are (a) ship Option C (no delegation at all, §10.1/§10.2 option (c)), or (b) hold Phase 2 until the SDK exposes either a verifier (branch V) or a genuinely resolved space id. Do not substitute a read-through-the-activated-handle check: §9.2 already records that that half SUCCEEDS FOR THE ATTACKER in T9's rebinding attack.
whatWASbuilt: Nothing that depends on this verdict. The in-process activation clamp (§3.2a edit 2) already refuses a tinycloud:-prefixed resource space that is not the delegation's own (portable-delegation.ts resourceSpaceWithinPolicy), and this fix round extended the same identity rule to the ACCEPT-side ceiling (foreignSpaceResources, wired into POST /api/delegations). That bounds what this process invokes and what it is willing to store. It is NOT the R10 control and must not be recorded as one: both of its sides still read the bundle's own declared spaceId, so it cannot tell a bundle that lies consistently from an honest one.

Flipping it without a re-run against a newer SDK is a reviewable lie in the diff.
